title: Rebase Board Filters Onto Main
description:
**SITUATION:**

Priya (or you earlier) pushed `feature/board-filters` to the forge — two commits that add board column filters (todo / doing / done / blocked) and a short README note. That tip lives on `origin`; your laptop starts on `main` and does not have a local copy of the feature yet.

While the feature sat there, `main` moved ahead on the forge (and on your local `main`): log level and a board_label helper, plus a README rewrite in the same boards section. The remote feature still starts from the older tip, so it is behind main.

Jordan blocked opening the PR this morning. On this team, feature branches stay **linear**: replay the two commits on current `main` — not a "Merge branch `main` into feature" knot. When the README commit replays, Git will stop; keep both your board-filters notes and `main`'s board_label note. Same subjects, new SHAs. Then push the rewritten feature (history changed, so a lease-safe force push). Do not change `main` yourself.

Your identity (Ada Learner) is already configured. Start on `main` in `~/sprint-service`; `origin` already points at the team forge.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Fetch from `origin` and check out `feature/board-filters` from the remote tip.
2. Replay that branch onto current `main` so it has exactly those two commits on top of `main`, with a linear history. Resolve the README conflict keeping both docs.
3. Push the rewritten `feature/board-filters` to `origin` (the history changed, so a normal push will be rejected — update the remote tip safely). Do not push or update `main`. Leave a clean working tree.

git rebase main — when README conflicts, keep board-filters docs and board_label, then git add README.md && git rebase --continue
Preserve the two original subjects. History is rewritten, so: git push --force-with-lease origin feature/board-filters

problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Rebase Board Filters Onto Main

Your `feature/board-filters` branch forked before `main` moved. Jordan wants a **linear** feature history for the PR — not a merge-of-main knot. Replay your two commits on top of today's `main`, resolve the README conflict by keeping **both** docs, then force-with-lease push the rewritten feature.

## 1. See the divergence

```bash
cd ~/sprint-service
git branch --show-current
git log --oneline --graph --all
```

Your two filter commits sit on an older tip; `main` has moved ahead. Origin already has that pre-rebase feature tip.

## 2. Rebase (do not merge)

```bash
git rebase main
```

The first commit (`filters.py`) applies cleanly. The second stops on `README.md` — both you and `main` rewrote the board docs.

## 3. Resolve README — keep both sides

Keep your board-filters usage notes **and** main's note about the `board_label` helper. Combine them; delete every conflict marker.

```bash
nano README.md
grep -nE '^(<<<<<<<|=======|>>>>>>>)' README.md   # should print nothing
git add README.md
git rebase --continue
```

Then confirm:

```bash
git log --oneline --graph --all
git log --oneline main..HEAD
```

Exactly two commits, same subjects, now based on main's tip. New SHAs are expected — that is rebase rewriting the feature tip.

## 4. Force-with-lease push the feature

Origin still points at the old tip. A plain push is rejected after rebase. Update **only** the feature branch:

```bash
git push --force-with-lease origin feature/board-filters
```

Do **not** push or rewrite `main`.

## Notes

- Merging `main` into the feature would sync the files but leave a merge commit; this lab wants the linear story.
- `git rebase --abort` undoes a rebase that went wrong.
- Leave `main` exactly where it is; only the feature branch should move.
- Never plain `--force` on a shared branch when `--force-with-lease` will do.
